messages:
Morgan: Heads up - ACME Data opened a high-priority support ticket. Their embedding ingestion started failing after we applied a pinned model for their Dedicated account. They report shape errors from their vector DB.

ACME Data: We had a nightly job that worked last night. After the pin went live this morning our ingestion pipeline started throwing errors. Sample error: "InvalidEmbeddingShape: got 1024, expected 1536". We haven't changed our schema.

Morgan: Can you paste the curl you used and a raw response body? Also confirm the model id you pinned to.

ACME Data: Here is what we ran:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-acme-v1","input":"hello world"}'
```

ACME Data: Response we logged (truncated):

{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [{"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.001, -0.002, ...], "index":0}],
  "model": "embed-acme-v1",
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens":2}
}

ACME Data: The array length in our logs is 1024. It used to be 1536. This breaks our DB ingestion. Need urgent help.

Sanjay: Tagging runtime. Two quick things to check: 1) did the pinned model switch to a different base that has a different vector size, 2) did batching or routing combine requests across model variants.

Elaine: Looking at the Dedicated control plane - the active instance for embed-acme-v1 is `embed-acme-v1@d-42` with metadata vector_size=1024 and base_model=lumina-compact-1. There was a maintenance change during the window that swapped in a compact variant to improve throughput.

Sanjay: That would explain the change in dimension. Immediate mitigations: we can either revert them to the previous instance or ask them to pause ingestion and reindex. For a quick customer-side safety net, suggest they assert len(embedding)==expected and drop/alert if not, and set client `max_batch_size=1` to avoid cross-variant coalescing.

ACME Data: We need ingestion back fast. We'll accept a short outage to revert.

Elaine: We have the previous snapshot `embed-acme-v1@d-41` available. I can schedule a re-pin and restart workers. ETA ~20-30 minutes, brief in-flight rejections expected. Initiating revert now.

infra-bot: Revert job 10077 initiated by Elaine. Provisioning nodes... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Sanjay: I'll open an action item to prevent silent dimensional changes on pinned models: require an explicit confirm flag or console acknowledgement for any pin that changes embedding_size. Also adding a runtime guard to reject batched requests that mix model instances.

Morgan: Support checklist for now: 1) check catalog or control-plane model.vector_size, 2) ask customer to run a simple curl to verify embedding length, 3) advise client-side batching toggle and length check, 4) if backup exists, offer revert and coordinate downtime, 5) coordinate reindex plan with customer.

infra-bot: Revert job 10077 complete. Active instance: embed-acme-v1@d-41, vector_size=1536. :white_check_mark:

ACME Data: Re-ran the curl, confirmed vectors are 1536 now. Ingestion resumed. Thanks for the quick help.

Elaine: Follow-ups created - INFRA-1001: pin audit and safe-revert playbook; ENG-2401: pin validation UI + API; SUPPORT-OPS-12: incident checklist.

Sanjay: Also adding a preflight endpoint so clients can fetch model metadata (embedding dim) before committing to a reindex or pin.

Morgan: Closing this thread. Will reopen if ACME sees further regressions. :v:
